short: Theodosius made Nicene Christianity the empire's compulsory state religion.
full:
Issued on 27 February 380 in the name of Theodosius I, Gratian and Valentinian II, the edict Cunctos populos ordered all subjects of the empire to follow the faith taught by the bishops of Rome and Alexandria, that is, Nicene Trinitarian Christianity, and named those who dissented as heretics rather than merely mistaken. It was the first law to designate one form of Christianity as the empire's official religion and to treat rival Christian sects, especially Arians, as legally deviant alongside pagans and Jews.

The edict did not itself outlaw pagan worship, which Theodosius targeted separately over the following decade, but it fused Roman citizenship with a specific creed for the first time. Enforcement followed quickly: Arian bishops were removed from major sees, and the Council of Constantinople in 381 confirmed Nicene orthodoxy as binding across the eastern empire.
